title: Hubble image of NGC 7714
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 7714, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: Ranked #90 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Strangely shaped arms and a smoky golden haze stretching from the centre give NGC 7714 an unsettled look in this Hubble image. This spiral lies 100 million light-years from Earth, in the constellation Pisces, a fairly close neighbour by cosmic standards.

Those distortions are signs of violent, dramatic events in the galaxy's recent past. NGC 7714 is in the midst of an ongoing merger with a smaller companion galaxy, NGC 7715, which lies outside the frame, and that encounter is behind both the odd arms and the golden haze.

Mergers are a common way for galaxies to change over time. As two galaxies pass close, their mutual gravity tugs on stars and gas, reshaping both, and over long periods they can combine into one. NGC 7714 offers a relatively nearby view of that process while it is still under way, with the smaller partner lying just beyond the edge of the picture.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.72 x 1.86 arcminutes) and distance (100 million light years), the frame spans roughly 79,000 × 54,000 light-years. Its light set out about 100 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3 observed in ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet and near-infrared parts of this light are invisible to the eye.
